decisions.recommendedDecision: Implement observer-only Azure identity normalization in a later repair/observer slice. Do not ALTER OWNER, GRANT/REVOKE, or rewrite ACLs on live Sunset merely to match local fixture role names.
evidence: Slice 13A classified 42 definition_mismatch rows as observer_normalization_difference (azuresu / azure_pg_admin vs $db_owner / pg_database_owner).
scripts/lib/sunset-schema-observer.js normalizeOwnerName only rewrites the connected datdba name to $db_owner; it does not map Azure Flexible Server system roles.
Product fingerprint excludes ledger; ownership presentation is environment identity, not tenant privilege model.

alternativesRejected.alternative: ALTER OWNER / ACL rewrite on live to match $db_owner
alternativesRejected.reason: Mutates Azure-managed identities; forbidden; does not improve product schema truth

alternativesRejected.alternative: Bless live owners into canonical fixture without normalization policy
alternativesRejected.reason: Would encode Azure-specific role names into canonical product contract and hide cross-env comparison
Could hide genuine privilege escalation or ACL broadenings

allowedSemanticEquivalenceMappings.condition: Only when the role is an Azure Flexible Server system superuser/extension owner and the privilege set being compared is ownership identity presentation — not EXECUTE/GRANT broadenings
Only when comparing public schema owner/grantor identity between Azure Flexible Server and local docker fixtures
Existing behavior: rewrite exact connected database owner name to $db_owner

forbidden: Treat PUBLIC or additional roles gaining SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/EXECUTE as equivalent
Collapse distinct privilege grants into a single owner token
Hide ACL widenings (extra grantees, broader privileges, WITH GRANT OPTION additions)
Normalize away ownership when live owner is a least-privilege app role that should not own extensions
Any SQL that ALTER OWNER / GRANT / REVOKE on live
normalizationPolicy.privilegeEscalationDetection: After identity normalization, ACL and ownership comparisons must still fail closed on grantee set expansion, privilege bit expansion, or owner moving from system/extension identity to an application login with broader effective rights than expected.

compatibilitySecurityConsequences.security: Reduces false-positive drift noise without mutating privileges; still detects ACL broadenings and unexpected owners

decisions.abortCondition: ABORT if proposed observer change would equate any ACL with strictly more grantees or privileges than expected after mapping, or if any mapping targets a non-allowlisted role name.
